Prevention: Raise seedlings in area free from the pest
Maintain the orchard using recommended cultural practices such as weeding, proper irrigation and fertilization
Spray the lower leaf surface infested with wwf with high pressure water using a horse pipe
Prune the lower branches to prevent their contact with the ground and ants because they can disrupt the natural control system
Monitoring: Monitor weekly and look for dense colonies of the immature whiteflies on the lower leaf surface look for wilting and dropping of leaves infested with
WWF Look for blackening on the leaves, twigs and fruit caused by sooty mould that grows on the honey dew secreted by the whitefly
Direct Control: Prune heavily infested leaves and branches and use as firewood or burn
Spray with soap solution (mixing 30ml of liquid soap with 15L water)
Introduce or conserve effective natural enemies of the whiteflies for biological control such as hymenopteran parasitoid
Hang yellow stick traps to reduce populations of adult whiteflies
Alternate row prunning to conserve natural enemies
Restrictions: No chemical pesticides are registered in
Ethiopia for the management of woolly whitefly on citrus
